title: County of Portugal
capsule: The County of Portucale (Condado de Portucale) was a frontier marquisate of the Kingdom of León established in the late ninth century to defend the Douro valley from Moorish raids; the Wikidata attestation from 1139 reflects the moment Afonso Henriques declared himself king after his victory at the Battle of Ourique (1139), effectively ending the county's subordinate status. Afonso had already been governing Portucale since c. 1128 after ousting his mother Teresa, who had aligned the county with Galicia. The Treaty of Zamora in 1143 received León's recognition of the new Portuguese kingdom, formally superseding the comital arrangement.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The county's territorial core around the Minho-Douro corridor is well established; the southern frontier fluctuated considerably with Reconquista campaigns and scholarly maps vary in detail.
